articles.title: ‘AGT’ Recap: Who Got Mel B.’s Live Golden Buzzer?
articles.summary: Night two of the Live Shows featured 11 more acts hitting the stage for a shot at the Semifinals.
articles.body:
The Quarterfinals continued on the August 25 episode of America's Got Talent . Eleven more acts took the stage in hopes of moving on in the competition.

Like last week, there was one Live Golden Buzzer in play. After Howie Mandel gave his to Hundred Fingers on August 18, sending them straight to the Finals, the power was in Mel B. 's hands this time around. America will vote for their favorites of the rest of the contestants, and three of those acts will move onto the Semifinals during tomorrow night's results show.

Because Simon Cowell is away from the show for a few weeks due to a "routine" procedure relating to his back injury , his seat was left empty, leaving Mandel, Mel, and Sofia Vergara to offer commentary from the judges' table.

Scroll down for a recap of the night's performances and to find out who got the Golden Buzzer.

Kicking off the night was LaRussell with a rap performance, accompanied by his friends from the Bay Area.

"First of all, I love what you guys stand for. I can feel the energy literally bouncing off the stage," Mel B. said. "I did find it a little bit chaotic. There was a lot going on. But like I said, your energy was right up there. It was. And that's the part that I enjoyed. I almost wish you had a few more days to rehearse it. I felt like you were a little bit out of breath, but I could feel the excitement."

The audience boo-ed Mel's response, but Vergara jumped in to say, "I do think this was a step up from the audition. I love it. I think it's amazing what they do." Finally, Mandel added, "I think it was good, I think it was entertaining. I don't know if it's at the level Season 21 is looking for. It felt like a musical recital from a high school to me."

The second performance was from aerialist Veronika Goroshkova, who was one of Vergara's Golden Buzzers during the Auditions. She did another wild routine, this time set to Taylor Swift 's "The Fate of Ophelia."

"Now you know why I gave her the Golden Buzzer. There is no one like her," Vergara raved. "The fascinating thing about me for you is you make it seem so easy, so effortless."

Mandel called Veronika "amazing" and said no other aerialist on the show has been as "graceful" as her. Mel B. added, "What else can I say? Everybody's said everything. You were that powerful, the sponge of my microphone popped off. Graceful. Just brilliant."

Just days after celebrating her 18th birthday, Bety hit the stage for a performance of TK TK. Bety was one of Mel B.'s callback acts who made the Quarterfinals after her second chance performance, and now her fate is in America's hands.

Bety sang Sam Smith's "Fire on Fire" for the Live Show. "You know I'm a massive fan of yours. Your voice is like velvet," Mel said. "I do think you played it a little bit too safe tonight. I know your vocal range is so wide, but it was beautiful."

Vergara told Bety she already looks like a "big star" on stage. "You wanted to do this your whole life and it shows in your performance. I love it," she gushed. Meanwhile, Mandel said Bety is "one of the best singers" on the season, but admitted, "That song doesn't have a ton of range. You have a ton of range. I love your audition so much more than this."

Come Here, a dance group, took the stage next. Heading into the big night, the group dealt with some setbacks as their choreographer had a prior commitment and couldn't make it to L.A. until just 12 hours before showtime.

The routine got a standing ovation from all three judges. "What a unique blend of contemporary and ballet, very original choreography," Mandel said. "You're amazing, you deserve to be here."

Vergara added, "Breathtaking. It was amazing. It was perfection. No tricks, no flips, it's just a unit." Mel B. said she thought the routine was "absolutely incredible," and it even seemed like she was going to press the Golden Buzzer for a second after a brief side conversation with Mandel. However, she held off for a future performance.

Music duo Nyjah Music and Zyah Rhythm were one of Cowell's callback acts. They came to the Live Shows hoping to show a new level of confidence with a performance of "I Swear."

The judges cringed through the performance, and Mel B. even hit her red buzzer to signify that she was not impressed. "You guys can sing, you can harmonize," Mandel began. "I think Simon said it in the package and I think he's right … it takes experience and time. I think you're going to be great. I think you're going to do well. But I feel it's just about experience. The nerves are kind of showing."

Mel B. said, "I actually felt I did you a favor. I think you need a lot more time, a lot more experience, and at this point in the competition, this should be your best. I should be able to feel the hunger, the passion. It was just like you were taking a walk on Malibu beach without a care in the world. I didn't see it." She urged the guys to practice and come back with "more determination."

Vergara had to agree with Mel and Mandel that Nyjah and Zyah played it too safe and needed more experience. "I think you need to keep working and follow your dream because you guys are good," she concluded.

Magician Geno Ploeger was up next. After previously working with AGT winner Mat Franco, Geno is now ready to make a name for himself. Mandel warned him during his audition that he needed to do something more original, and he came ready to show that off.

"I don't even have words," Mel B. said afterwards. Vergara raved, "This was original. I'm so glad you paid attention to what Howie told you. This feels like you. It suits you. This is how you have to keep doing it."

Finally, Mandel gushed, "I said if you come back, you do you, something I have never seen. You. Did. You."

Cowell called Patrox "one of the most original acts we've ever seen" when he auditioned, and he showed off his unique backwards dance skills once again.

"I think it's so clever what you do. I don't really fully understand what the hell is happening, but it's fun," Vergara said. "To make something like that work on a stage like this is not easy."

Mel B. admitted she liked that Patrox is "so excited," but again, she said she didn't understand the concept of his dancing and backwards replay. Mandel jumped in to say, "I think what you do is incredibly unique. It's a trick. It's an amazing trick. I applaud you."

Teenage rocker Nene Royal took the stage next. After getting through to the Quarterfinals as one of Mandel's callback acts, she was ready to prove she belonged, especially since her audition went so viral.

Is she wearing a painted t-shirt with her own name on it? #AGT pic.twitter.com/Bx9hfM03iq — AGT Time Podcast (@agttimepod) August 26, 2026

Is she wearing a painted t-shirt with her own name on it? #AGT pic.twitter.com/Bx9hfM03iq

After Nene's performance of "Black Hole Sun" by Soundgarden, Mandel addressed NBC directly, saying, "Give her the $1 million. Right now!" Vergara said, "I think you can really win this competition. You can sing and play that guitar. No wonder everybody on the street asks me about you!"

Mel could barely get a word in edgewise over the loud screams of the audience. "You are just the most humblest, sweet, young lady, and then you come out on this stage and it's a different vibe," she applauded.

Vergara urged her to push the Golden Buzzer, and Mel B. said, "I love really good vocals. I'm a 90s girl. I'm into pop music. That kind of music is not my vibe. But your vocals are on point, your guitar is on point, your look, your energy, your vibe … how could I not do this?!" And with that, Nene is in the Finals!

Mackenzie Sol , one of Mel B.'s audition Golden Buzzers, returned to the stage next. He wanted to do something different for the Live Shows, so he sang Tate McRae's "You Broke Me First," and got emotional at the end of the performance.

"That was so good," Mel B. promised. "That was everything. The feelings, the trills, the vocals, the voice, the everything. That was just … yeah." Vergara told Mackenzie, "I think the girls are going to go crazy with you. So handsome, such a beautiful energy, such a beautiful voice. I loved your audition and I love you tonight."

Mandel said she hopes people vote for Mackenzie, and Mel jumped in to add, "I really, really, really hope people vote for you!" Mandel also made sure Mackenzie knew he "rose to the occasion" of having to perform after Nene.

Extreme danger act (and married couple) Brad and Tracy came with another death-defying routine next. Mel was so grossed out by Brad's sword-swallowing trick that she pushed her red buzzer and turned away.

The act did not quite resonate and fell very flat, although Mandel did give a standing ovation. "The energy and the showmanship … you cant even put into words what we just saw," he said. "It is so bad, it is amazing."

Vergara added, "I could not stop thinking about what your neighbors think about you two. You guys are scary. Tracy, you should be in a scary movie. You're perfect, your acting, your delivery. It's amazing. I don't know if this is good, if it's bad. We can't stop looking at you guys, so I guess it's a good thing."

Mel admitted that "this is a genre where people do things to themselves like that," but said, "I find it more comedic. I do like the vibe. But just … why?"

The final performance of the night was from singing duo Butter and Grit.

"Your vocals have got exponentially more than amazing. That song, and it's an original … I love your friendship, I love your vibe, America needs to vote for you," Mel B. gushed.

What Is 'AGT' Finalist Preacher Lawson Doing Now?

Vergara said she loved Butter and Grit's original songs. "They feel like they're already hits, that they've been hits. I really love your friendship and relationship," she added. Mandel concluded, "There's nothing more America than that type of music and the way you sing it."

articles.title: Hearing tech startup Legato emerges from stealth with $12M and a peek at its AI hearing glasses | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The glasses, called Legato Frames, integrate the company’s patented hearing-assistance technology into the arms of eyewear frames.
articles.body:
Hearing loss affects an estimated 50 million adults in the United States, but only around 20% of those with diagnosed hearing loss seek treatment. Legato , a new hearing tech company, aims to close that gap.

The startup is emerging from stealth on Wednesday with $12 million in funding and a first look at its AI hearing glasses, the company told TechCrunch exclusively. The glasses, called Legato Frames, integrate the company’s patented hearing-assistance technology into the arms of eyewear frames. Legato Frames are expected to launch later this fall.

Legato was founded by Mehul Trivedi and Steve Romine, who bring extensive experience in wearables and hearing care from Bose, where Trivedi led the creation of Bose Frames and Romine ran the hearing aids division. Trivedi left Bose to work at EssilorLuxottica, where he led smart eyewear efforts and worked on the Meta Ray-Bans, while Romine went on to serve as COO of hearing care company Audicus.

After spending years at larger companies, Trivedi took some time off to explore the intersection of hearing technology and smart eyewear. During that time, Trivedi came across technology he believed could bring the two together, so he contacted Romine and the pair founded Legato in late 2024.

“Our goal is to make hearing as ubiquitous as vision,” Trivedi said in an interview with TechCrunch. “It’s kind of a no-brainer that you go to an eye exam, you get your glasses, you wear your glasses, and you’re happy, and you do that for the rest of your life — and the idea of it being blurry again where you would just stop wearing them is not a consideration. I think that’s what we want to do with hearing: just make it something that people address and almost forget about.”

Legato is targeting people with mild to moderate hearing loss, which represents the largest segment of the hearing-loss population, the startup says.

The company started with the goal of making hearing care more accessible by addressing the cost, comfort, and stigma associated with traditional hearing aids. Legato set out to make the glasses as small and lightweight as possible, and developed a proprietary acoustic system, signal-processing stack, and mechanical architecture to achieve it.

Traditional hearing aids often use directional microphones to focus on sounds coming from a particular direction, which works well in quiet settings but can be difficult in noisy environments, such as restaurants. Legato takes a different approach by using an AI-powered system to differentiate between background noise and voices, amplifying only the voices.

The goal is to make conversations clearer without creating the cognitively draining listening experience that can come with some traditional hearing aids.

“We wanted to deliver an experience that was unique,” Trivedi said. “So a form factor that’s really discreet and looks normal. They’re meant to feel and look like regular glasses. And so, we want it to be a product that’s effortless, easy to use, with kind of no controls that you need to fiddle with, works everywhere, works throughout your day, doesn’t need a ton of configuration, and just delivers you better hearing.”

While the frames have an open-ear design, sound isn’t broadcast to people around you. They feature a dual-speaker system that directs sound toward the wearer while canceling sound that escapes, reducing sound by 99% just a few inches away from the ear.

The company’s funding, which is from Neotribe Ventures, Listen, and Village Global, has largely gone toward product development, along with marketing efforts.

“We have an opportunity to address a population with this product and build something that delivers without all the compromises of traditional hearing aids,” Trivedi said. “Hearing, at first glance, it’s not so much just like ‘I want to hear the TV better.’ It’s really about connection. When you hear better, you connect to the world. It reduces dementia risk and depression risk,” he continued.

“There’s impactful hearing health factors associated with better hearing. We’ve got a product that lives on people for 16 hours that is trusted to help them with their hearing and their vision, and we’d love to continue helping them in every way we can.”

When the frames launch later this year, Legato says they’ll be available through select eye-care providers nationwide and will “cost a fraction” of traditional hearing aids and may be eligible for vision insurance when purchased through an eye-care clinic.

articles.title: Volvo’s cars will warn one another about hazards in the road
articles.summary: Volvo’s connected safety alerts will now warn drivers when there are animals, pedestrians, cyclists, roadwork, or accidents ahead.
articles.body: Volvo is updating three of its electric vehicles with new hazard alerts to warn drivers when there are animals or vulnerable road users ahead. The new connected safety features are based on Volvo’s cars talking to one another, as opposed to crowdsourced alert systems used by popular navigation tools like Google Maps and Waze. The alerts work by using connected vehicle data from Volvo’s fleet of passenger vehicles in Europe, the US, and Canada. The car’s sensors and cameras are tuned to identify certain risks on the road. When one Volvo spots a hazard, it automatically logs the location and sends it to Volvo’s servers. Alerts are then sent to all other Volvo vehicles traveling along that same road. The alerts still depend on the car being connected to the cloud and the road existing in the map database, but Volvo’s newer EVs have plenty of computing power to handle the real-time processing requests. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Volvo said it’s updating its EVs with alerts for four types of hazards: large animals; vulnerable road users, like pedestrians or cyclists; roadwork; and accidents. The new alerts are coming to the Volvo EX90, ES90, and EX60. Volvo says it has 1 million vehicles on the road today with connected safety alert capabilities. And it shares its alert data with traffic management centers, as well as other vehicle brands, so its not just Volvo branded vehicles that are benefiting. Volvo has used connected vehicle technology to power some of its hazard warnings since 2016. The Swedish company’s cloud-based system, developed in partnership with Ericsson, warns drivers of slippery roads ahead based on feedback from steering, braking, and acceleration sensors. It also notifies nearby vehicles when another car has activated its hazard lights indicating that another driver may be in a dangerous or unexpected position on the road. In addition, Volvo said that the EX90 would be getting Spatial Audio support for Apple CarPlay users. This will allow drivers to “enjoy a multi-dimensional and immersive sound experience that places music and vocals around the cabin,” the company says.

articles.title: Apple is holding its iPhone launch event on September 9 | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The event is expected to be a notable one, as Apple is rumored to unveil its long-awaited foldable iPhone. It'll also be the first Apple event with John Ternus as CEO, who is scheduled to take the reins of the tech giant from Tim Cook on September 1.
articles.body:
Apple announced on Wednesday that its next launch event is taking place on September 9, with a “Surprise and Shine” tagline.

The event is expected to be a notable one, as Apple is rumored to unveil its long-awaited foldable iPhone. It’ll also be the first Apple event with John Ternus as CEO. Ternus is scheduled to take the reins of the tech giant from Tim Cook on September 1.

Apple is expected to announce the new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, but the two models are rumored to be relatively iterative upgrades rather than a major redesign. Reports have indicated that the company won’t be announcing the standard iPhone 18 until next year .

The tech giant is also expected to introduce the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra, alongside new smart home devices.

In addition to the new hardware, the company may announce launch dates for iOS 27, iPadOS 27, macOS Golden Gate, and other upcoming software updates.

The event will take place at the Apple Park Campus in Cupertino, California at 10 am PT.

articles.title: The Apple event is confirmed for September 9: New foldable iPhone Ultra, iPhone 18 Pro lineup and more we expect
articles.summary: Curious about what Apple may launch at its next iPhone event? Here's what we expect to see, from a folding iPhone to the new iPhone 18 Pro series and beyond.
articles.body:
Apple has officially confirmed its next iPhone launch event is on September 9 , putting it just under two weeks away. That means we're closer than ever to getting our first official look at what the company has been working on. Fortunately (or unfortunately if you're Apple), there have been a lot of leaks and rumors ahead of the event that indicate it'll be packed to the gills with some exciting launches.

This year, we expect to see Apple unveil the new iPhone 18 series, but it's increasingly looking like the company will join Samsung in offering a foldable phone of its own. That would be big enough to carry an event on its own, but we suspect Apple has quite a bit more stuff to show off at its September iPhone event. Here's a look at everything we're expecting to see.

Finally, a folding iPhone (iPhone Ultra?)

Apple has been slow to jump on the foldable phone bandwagon, but this may be the year it finally does. Rumors and purported details about the phone have been swirling for months, and we have a pretty good idea of what it might look like. A leaked dummy model shows a shorter, wider device than typical foldables of years past, looking remarkably similar to the recently launched Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 .

Other rumors suggest that the phone will sport a 5.5-inch front screen and a 7.8-inch display when open. With a 4:3 aspect ratio, it should look similar to an iPad Mini when open. That should make it better than taller foldables for consuming media, with smaller black bars when watching videos on the inner screen.

Samsung is reportedly making the OLED screens for the foldable iPhone, which would make sense given its extensive experience with foldable displays. The body of the phone is also rumored to be made from titanium and aluminum, with a liquid-metal hinge that should hold up better to wear over time.

There's also the name of the foldable to consider. Most rumors point to iPhone Ultra, though it's unclear if that will be the final name at launch.

Don't expect a wide range of colors for Apple's first foldable. The iPhone Ultra is expected to come in only two colors, according to a May rumor : white and indigo. It's also likely to be in low supply, with leakers suggesting it may only launch in the U.S. initially, with more territories to come as production ramps up.

Given the state of the global memory shortage (or RAMageddon ) and the advanced manufacturing involved, expect the foldable iPhone to be pretty expensive. No exact pricing has been confirmed, but it's widely expected to be north of $2,000 . That could be one of the main reasons behind the recent launch of Apple's Upgrade leasing program .

The design of the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are largely expected to be very similar to last year's iPhone 17 Pro series. However, new colors are reportedly on the way , including a dark cherry hue that may sit alongside a light blue color, dark gray and silver. Otherwise, expect the same aluminum finish as the current model, though the ceramic shield may get a frosted look.

Where the iPhone 18 Pro models could get a major upgrade is in their main camera sensors. In a blog post , Apple analyst Ming-Chi Kuo said that the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max may get variable-aperture main cameras that can control the amount of light that reaches the sensor on the fly. This would be a first for iPhones, and could give users greater control over the depth of field in their photos.

As you'd expect, the iPhone 18 Pro series is expected to see an updated main processing chip. This year it should be the A20, which will be built on a process that should bring more power efficiency and performance. However, exact details on how much more efficient it may be aren't available right now.

Other rumors suggest the camera control button could be simplified by removing touch sensitivity and haptic feedback. The Dynamic Island may get smaller as well, as a portion of the Face ID module may be moved under the display.

Given Apple already pushed through price increases on its Macs and iPads earlier this year, it's likely we'll see pricing on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max increase as well. However, we won't know until Apple debuts them on stage.

Apple has been on a more iterative update cadence for its Apple Watch models for the past several years, and it looks like this year will be the same. According to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman , Apple is planning to launch the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 at its September event. Gurman notes that they're expected to get "under-the-hood improvements" to give them a boost in performance.

There should also be new colors and bands, according to the report, along with some "health and fitness-related upgrades." One wild card is whether we'll see the return of the high-end ceramic case version of the Apple Watch. Gurman says Apple is planning for one, but it isn't clear if it'll arrive this year or in 2027.

A new HomePod, Apple TV 4K, and … a home hub?

If you're a fan of Apple's home-centric devices, this year's iPhone launch event should be pretty interesting. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman claims that the company is preparing to launch a new HomePod Mini and an updated Apple TV 4K set-top box. It might also preview the smart home hub it has been rumored to be working on for a couple of years now.

The home hub would be the biggest draw. According to Gurman, the device features a 7-inch screen that sits on top of what looks like half of a HomePod Mini. It's rumored to run a new operating system that's built off of the Apple TV OS, and it should give you access to smart home controls, your calendar, photos, music, apps and a customizable clock.

The rumored hub is said to be built with the new, smarter AI Siri in mind, acting as an assistant when you need it. Gurman also says facial recognition is a big part of this device's appeal, allowing it to determine who is looking at it to serve up personalized content. He adds that it can determine your distance from the display and adjust the size of what's displayed in response.

Gurman says Apple is also working on a second version of the hub that's meant to be mounted on a wall as well, though it's unclear if it's meant to launch at the same time.

As for the HomePod Mini and Apple TV 4K, they should look like the current versions that are already available. The biggest difference is that they'll contain more powerful processors to power the new Siri AI experience.

While the above products cover most of what we expect to see at Apple's September event, we've seen leaks and hints of other devices that could be in the pipeline. It's not guaranteed they'll be present at the iPhone event, but we could see them launched in the following months.

One of the most anticipated products is a new iPad Mini with an OLED screen . It's also expected to feature a water-resistant design for the first time. Both upgrades would make this the biggest update to the iPad Mini since it got a design overhaul in 2021 (though it was updated with a faster processor in 2024). It's unclear if we'll see this at the iPhone event since it's rumored to launch in October, but it's a possibility.

Apple is also said to be working on a new set of AirPods Pro that incorporates visual sensors to feed Siri information about the world around you. A short demo video featuring the new AirPods recently leaked in a beta build of macOS Tahoe , which hints that they're close to launch. However, Bloomberg claims that they're targeted for a 2027 release, so we might not see them at this iPhone event.

When is the September 2026 iPhone launch, and how can I watch?

The event is officially confirmed to kick off on September 9 at 1 p.m. ET (10 a.m. PT). As for how to watch the event, Apple typically streams its launches on YouTube, on its website and through the Apple TV app. We'll update this post with more details as we get them.

articles.title: Apple Maps has ads now
articles.summary: Ads are starting to show up in the Apple Maps iPhone app, at the top of search results and suggested places labeled with an “ad” icon.
articles.body: Ads have started popping up in Apple Maps, following Apple’s announcement in March that it would let businesses pay for top spots. They’re appearing on my iPhone as the first entry in the “suggested places” section in search, but Apple says they’ll also show up at the top of search results. According to 9to5Mac, the ads began rolling out this week, and more users in the US and Canada will start seeing them over the next few weeks. They’re marked with a blue “ad” icon, similar to the ads Google’s had in its Maps app for years now. I was also greeted with a pop-up warning me about the ads when I launched the Maps app this morning: > Maps may show local ads based on your approximate location, current search terms, or view of the map while you search. For your privacy, advertising information is not linked to your Apple Account. Apple shared similar privacy claims in its March announcement for the ads, stating, “A user’s location and the ads they see and interact with in Maps are not associated with a user’s Apple Account. Personal data stays on a user’s device, is not collected or stored by Apple, and is not shared with third parties.”

articles.title: The Switch 2’s $50 price increase is happening next week
articles.summary: Just a reminder that Nintendo’s Switch 2 will cost $499.99 instead of its usual $449.99 price starting September 1st.
articles.body: This is a friendly reminder that the Nintendo Switch 2 will jump in price by $50 starting on September 1st. That’s next Tuesday! The company gave plenty of notice, but the time has finally come. The base 256GB model that ships without a game will go from $449.99 to $499.99. Nintendo recently announced two bundles (both well over $500) shipping this fall that include a game with a slight discount. If you’re on the fence for a Switch 2, now is a pretty good time to buy one — not just because of the upcoming price increase. The game library is stellar and growing quickly, and the console itself is great, too. You’ll need one to play the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, The Duskbloods, and plenty of other upcoming games. Alas, no tech product will escape RAMageddon unscathed, especially one like the Switch 2 that has speedy RAM and storage. Almost all competing handhelds cost more than before, too, though Nintendo’s $50 price increase is soft compared to the $200-plus increase for the Steam Deck OLED . articles.title: Apple iPhone Event Invites Have Gone Out, and I Want a Foldable iPhone
articles.summary: There are a few things that are inevitable every year, and one of those is that Apple is going to host a big, flashy event in September to show off its new iPhone. And now, Apple has announced a September 9 event that'll do just that.
articles.body:
There are a few things that are inevitable every year, and one of those things is Apple hosting a big, flashy event in September to show off its newest iPhone. And now, Apple has announced a September 9 event that'll do just that.

The event will happen September 9 at 10am PST, and while the company hasn't shared exactly what's in store, it's not hard to guess that this is where all the latest iPhones are going to get showcased. As for which iPhones will be getting a refresh, its anyone's guess, but it's safe to assume that the iPhone 18 and its Pro version will be there, along with the latest Apple Watch.

But rumors have circled for ages that Apple has been toying with the idea of launching a foldable phone. It feels like this is something that I've been hearing for years now, but with how far foldables have come in the last two years, specifically, this could be the year that Apple finally brings its version to the masses – after all, it has named this iteration of the event "Surprise and Shine." A foldable iPhone would certainly be surprising, to say the least.

Back in July, Apple analyst Ming-Chi Quo predicted that the foldable iPhone would be coming sometime this year, but that it would be in limited supply, with "7–8 million units, with 3Q26 shipments at 0.5–1 million units, or about 10% of the total." He also predicted that if the foldable is real, it'd be quite expensive. That shouldn't be surprising, though, with the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra costing $2,100 when it launched last month.

While that would mean Apple would be quite late to the foldable game, the company has a track record of taking technologies and launching them into the stratosphere. It's hard to imagine that a $2,000 phone is going to have mainstream success, but if any company could do it, it'd be Apple.

Beyond the rumored foldable, though, I don't suspect that the iPhone 18 and 18 Pro are going to be that different from the iPhone 17 . The 17 Pro brought a new chassis, with a much better camera shelf, and I'd expect Apple to ride that chassis out for another year.

Whichever iPhones Apple elects to launch this year will probably come with a modest price bump, though. The RAM crisis does apply to phones, and the company has already raised prices on the rest of its product lineup . It wouldn't be surprising, then, that the new iPhone is going to have at least some price increase baked in. At least that would help the company avoid raising prices on older products.
